name: How do you keep water from flooding the bathroom without a shower curb?

mainEntity.name: How do you keep water from flooding the bathroom without a shower curb?

acceptedAnswer.text: Water is contained through precise subfloor sloping, targeted drain placement, and strategic showerhead direction. The floor must slope downward toward the drain at a minimum pitch of one-quarter inch per foot so water clears rapidly. Linear drains installed against the back wall or across the entrance offer superior water containment compared to traditional center point drains. While open walk-in designs are popular, adding fixed glass splash panels helps shield vanity areas and drying zones from overspray. During planning, you must weigh the sleek openness of a completely doorless layout against the risk of minor overspray during high-pressure showers.
acceptedAnswer.description: Water is contained by sloping the floor inward toward the drain, installing high-capacity linear drains, and placing glass splash panels to block spray.
